title: "Response feature analysis"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Response feature analysis}

  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Response feature analysis is a two-stage approach for analyzing longitudinal tumor growth data. It summarizes each subject's growth trajectory using an interpretable response feature and compares these features across treatment groups.

The `rfeat()` function implements this approach by estimating subject-specific growth slopes and performing statistical comparisons between treatment groups.

## Preparing the data

We use the `melanoma2` dataset included with the package.

```{r}
library(tumr)
data("melanoma2")

melanoma2$months <- melanoma2$Day / (365 / 12)
mel2 <- tumr(melanoma2, ID, months, Volume, Treatment)
```

## Fitting response feature analysis

The `rfeat()` function:

1. Estimates a growth slope for each subject.
2. Summarizes the slopes within each treatment group.
3. Performs statistical comparisons between groups.

Available comparisons include t-tests, ANOVA, Tukey post-hoc tests, and a combination of ANOVA and Tukey tests.

The following example uses `comparison = "both"` to perform ANOVA and Tukey post-hoc comparisons.

```{r}
rfeat_mel2 <- rfeat(mel2, comparison = "both")
rfeat_mel2
```

## Visualizing response features

The `plot()` method displays individual subject slopes and group-level mean estimates.

```{r}
plot(rfeat_mel2)
```

This visualization provides a convenient way to examine variation in tumor growth rates across subjects and treatment groups.
